extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate or graduate students and instructors in complex analysis / geometric topology
extracted.subtask_description: Proofs and supporting lemmas for the Jordan curve theorem for simple piecewise-smooth curves, plus consequences such as Cauchy's theorem on integrals over such curves; includes construction of parallel translates, winding-number arguments, and local geometric estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cauchy theorem in simply connected interior (Theorem 2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose f is a function that is holomorphic in the interior Omega of a simple closed curve Gamma. Then the integral of f over any closed curve eta contained in Omega is 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a direct corollary of the simply-connectedness of the interior: any closed curve in Omega is homotopic to a point in Omega and hence the integral vanishes. Used as a building block for later general Cauchy theorem statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of disjoint parallel translates (Lemma 2.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Gamma0 be a simple smooth curve with arc-length parametrization gamma:[0,L]->C. For each real epsilon, define gamma_epsilon(t)=gamma(t)+i*epsilon*gamma'(t). Then there exists kappa1>0 so that Gamma0 intersect Gamma_epsilon = empty whenever 0 < |epsilon| < kappa1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses uniform continuity of gamma' on [0,L] and local estimates: for small parameter differences |t-s| one gets a lower bound proportional to |epsilon|. Globally one covers [0,L] by small intervals and uses minimum distance between compact pieces. This provides the basic 'parallel curve' construction used throughout the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of near points as parallel translates (Lemma 2.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If z is a point not on a smooth curve Gamma0 and its closest point on Gamma0 is an interior point z0 = gamma(t0) with t0 in (0,L), then z = gamma(t0) + i*epsilon*gamma'(t0) for some epsilon != 0 (i.e., z lies on a parallel translate of Gamma0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses differentiability of gamma at interior points and the fact that z0 minimizes distance to z; orthogonality condition yields the scalar epsilon. This justifies the local picture that points near an interior point of Gamma0 lie on one of the parallel translates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Same-side / opposite-side criterion (definition and usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: If z in Gamma_epsilon and w in Gamma_eta for nonzero epsilon and eta, then z and w are said to be on the same side of Gamma0 when epsilon and eta have the same sign, and on opposite sides when the signs differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is only a relative notion (it does not globally define two sides of Gamma0). It is used to decide whether points can be joined by a curve running 'parallel' to Gamma0 or whether one must go around an endpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joining nearby points on the same side (Proposition 2.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A and B be the endpoints of a simple smooth curve Gamma0, and let K be a compact set with either Gamma0 intersect K = empty or Gamma0 intersect K = A union B. If z,w not on Gamma0 lie on the same side of Gamma0 and are closer to interior points of Gamma0 than to K or the endpoints, then z and w can be joined by a continuous curve lying entirely in the complement of K union Gamma0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: connect z and w to nearby points on a single parallel translate Gamma_epsilon with small epsilon (using line segments to the translate which avoid K union Gamma0), then follow the appropriate segment of Gamma_epsilon between those points. Choose epsilon smaller than kappa1 and the distance to K on the relevant segment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of half-neighborhood around an endpoint (Lemma 2.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a simple smooth curve Gamma0 there exists kappa2>0 so that the set N = { z = gamma(L) + epsilon*e^{i theta}*gamma'(L) : -pi/2 <= theta <= pi/2, 0 < epsilon < kappa2 } is disjoint from Gamma0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a 'half-neighborhood' near an endpoint where one may route curves to go around the endpoint while staying disjoint from the curve. Proof similar to Lemma 2.4 using local estimates and choosing kappa2 smaller than distance to the rest of the curve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joining points on opposite sides by routing around an endpoint (Proposition 2.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be an endpoint of Gamma0 and K a compact set with Gamma0 intersect K = empty or = A. If z,w not on Gamma0 are closer to interior points of Gamma0 than to K or to endpoints, then z and w can be joined by a continuous curve in the complement of Gamma0 union K (even if z and w lie on opposite sides).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline: connect z and w to translates that lead toward the endpoint A, then join within the half-neighborhood N of Lemma 2.7, choosing epsilon small relative to kappa1, kappa2 and distances to K. This handles the 'go around the end' case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boundary-of-complement equals the curve; connectedness of complement for arc/chain (component result used in proof of Theorem 2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a simple piecewise-smooth curve Gamma, the boundary of O = Gamma^c is precisely Gamma. If Gamma is a simple smooth arc (or a union of such arcs with suitable intersections), the complement is connected (proved by induction on number of smooth pieces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key idea: any two points outside Gamma can be joined by a curve which, if it intersects Gamma, can be modified using Propositions 2.6 and 2.8 by traveling along parallel translates and around endpoints. Induction adds one smooth segment at a time and uses compactness of the union of previously handled segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jordan curve theorem for piecewise-smooth curves (Theorem 2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Gamma is a simple, closed, piecewise-smooth curve, then its complement consists of exactly two components: an unbounded component U with winding number 0 and a bounded interior component Omega with winding number 1. The curve Gamma is the common boundary of both components, and the interior Omega is simply connected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof ingredients: define U as the set of points joinable to a fixed far point without crossing Gamma; show Omega = Gamma^c minus U is connected by using Propositions 2.6/2.8 on a deleted smooth piece; show existence of points with different winding numbers by evaluating near a smooth point and comparing the winding numbers of points on opposite sides (limit computation gives difference 1); finally show Omega is simply connected by contradiction using components and connectedness of U.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local winding-number jump equals one near a smooth point (winding-number computation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a smooth point gamma(t0) on Gamma and small epsilon>0, the two nearby points z_epsilon = gamma(t0) + i*epsilon*gamma'(t0) and w_epsilon = gamma(t0) - i*epsilon*gamma'(t0) lie on opposite sides and their winding numbers with respect to Gamma differ by 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the difference of Cauchy integrals for the two points and localize the integral near t0; after change of variables t-t0 = epsilon*s the leading integral tends to 1 as epsilon -> 0, while the remainder goes to 0. This yields the crucial topological distinction between the two sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Cauchy theorem for simple closed piecewise-smooth curves (Theorem 2.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is holomorphic in an open set that contains a simple closed piecewise-smooth curve Gamma and its interior, then the integral of f over Gamma is 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct a closed curve Lambda contained entirely in the interior Omega and arbitrarily close to Gamma by using parallel translates near smooth parts (Lemma 2.4) and small circular arcs at the join points (Lemma 2.10). Cover Gamma by a chain of small discs inside the holomorphic domain, build Lambda inside them, note f has primitives on those discs (since Omega is simply connected), so the integral over Lambda is 0; letting Lambda approach Gamma shows the integral over Gamma is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circle meets curve once near endpoint (Lemma 2.10, technical arc-joining)
rubrics_metrics.description: If gamma:[0,1]->C is a simple smooth curve, then for all sufficiently small delta>0 the circle centered at gamma(0) of radius delta intersects gamma in precisely one point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses smoothness and the mean value theorem applied to h(t)=|gamma(t)|^2: multiple intersections arbitrarily near the endpoint would force gamma'(0)·gamma(0)=0 for small parameters, contradicting gamma'(0) != 0. This lemma is used to select small circular arcs around join points to connect parallel translates when building the curve Lambda.
